text:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME (prod private deployment, us-west-2) started seeing API TLS handshake timeouts after DX maintenance ~08:10 UTC. 502s from our private endpoint.
kevin_neteng: noted. any packet captures or error snippets from the customer?
julia_acme: logs show repeated TLS timeout + ECONNRESET. also BGP flaps on their side after the provider change. we tried curl and it hangs on TLS handshake.
ops_richard: oncall-bot pushed an alert for route missing for 10.234.0.0/24 from ACME VPC. could be routing or firewall.
oncall-bot: alert: private-api-prod (svc-id: p-xxxx) health failing; rate 88% TLS timeouts. linked runbook: /runbooks/private-peering
kevin_neteng: please run a traceroute from their VPC to our private IP and get a tcpdump on the customer firewall for ESP/UDP 4500/500. ask them to run `dig @10.0.0.2 private-api.internal +short` too.
julia_acme: attaching outputs: 

```
$ traceroute -n 10.234.0.12
 1  10.0.1.1  0.78 ms
 2  192.0.2.5  2.11 ms
 3  198.51.100.2  5.22 ms
 4  * * *
```
and tcpdump for ike/4500/esp shows only UDP/500 traffic, no 4500 and no proto 50.
```
09:03:21.123 IP 198.51.100.10.500 > 198.51.100.2.500: IKEv2
09:03:27.456 IP 198.51.100.10.500 > 198.51.100.2.500: IKEv2
# no UDP/4500 observed
```
maria_support: interesting - if NAT-T (4500) isn't present but NAT exists in path, ESP (proto 50) will fail. ask them if any egress allowlist/firewall rules were tightened during maintenance.
julia_acme: their infra team says they only allowed UDP/500 and ICMP; they blocked other IP protocols and blocked UDP 4500 for some security policy change earlier today.
kevin_neteng: that matches symptoms. when NAT exists between peers we rely on NAT-T (UDP/4500). blocking 4500 and ESP can cause IKE to stay on 500 but child SA (ESP) will be unroutable or dropped -> TLS sessions from app hang.
ops_richard: also saw BGP adjacency drop during the window; provider and customer DX path briefly moved traffic over a transit link that didn't allow protocol 50. that caused asymmetric return path.
kevin_neteng: ask customer to temporarily allow outbound UDP/4500 and IP protocol 50 (ESP) to our peer addresses and keep UDP/500. also check MTU (fragmentation can break TLS over IPsec if DF set). run:
```
# on customer edge
sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 198.51.100.2 and \(udp port 500 or udp port 4500 or proto 50\)
# check MTU
ip link show dev eth0
```
maria_support: customer patched their egress allowlist to permit UDP/4500 + proto 50, also bumped MTU on the DX interface from 1500->9000? they said jumbo frames were enabled during maintenance and we think a mismatch caused fragmentation.
julia_acme: tested after rules change — `openssl s_client -connect 10.234.0.12:443 -timeout 5` now completes TLS handshake. API health back to normal for a subset of requests.
kevin_neteng: we still need to verify symmetric routing for ESP. provider (aws-dx-bot) — can you confirm the DX path for ACME now uses consistent next-hop and isn't performing ECMP to a transit that blocks proto 50?
aws-dx-bot: DX route table: virtual-interface vif-abc - primary path to 198.51.100.0/24 -> direct to core-usw2-a. ECMP not in effect. BGP session stable.
ops_richard: rolled a canary and monitor — 15m of stable TLS handshakes and no BGP flaps so far.
maria_support: customer will keep rules open for 24h and coordinate with their security team to add explicit permit for ESP/UDP4500 to our peer IPs. sending remediation checklist and runbook steps.
kevin_neteng: postmortem items: (1) add check to validator to flag firewall allowlists blocking UDP/4500/ESP for private deployments, (2) update private onboarding doc to call out MTU/jumbo frame risks with DX, (3) add a healthcheck that verifies NAT-T negotiation sees UDP/4500 packets.
julia_acme: thanks team — ACME folks confirmed resolution from their side as well. will re-close after 24h observation.
ops_richard: closing interim incident but leaving thread open until final confirmation.
